clue.text: Festivity with experienced knight

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
had means underwent or experienced, as in 'had a fright'

explanation.surface: A party attended by a seasoned knight of the realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad is the purest of King Arthur's Round Table knights, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Young earl in Sandwich area under protection

parts.note: green means young and inexperienced

indicators.note: in means the earl letter is put inside the sandwich

parts.note: a BLT is a bacon, lettuce and tomato sandwich

explanation.surface: A young Earl of Sandwich is kept under protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The Earl of Sandwich is a real title, but here 'Sandwich' is just a BLT. A green belt is land around a British town kept free of building.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names a ring of countryside around a town where development is restricted.

clue.text: Cover swollen scapula partially

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A swollen shoulder blade is partly covered up.
explanation.definitionFit: The cap that fits over a camera lens is a protective covering for the glass.

clue.text: Special issue of 'Tunes' picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a microphone picks up a sound, so the word is as spoken

parts.note: airs are tunes or melodies

explanation.surface: A special edition of a magazine called Tunes is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a magazine edition, but it means offspring; 'Special issue' is children marked out to inherit.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means children or descendants, and those designated to inherit are a special class of them.

clue.text: Cook sent lad eggs stuffed with extremely oaten fillers

indicators.note: cook means the letters of sent lad are cooked up into a new order
stuffed with means the urging word is filled with the outer letters

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them

indicators.note: extremely means the two end letters of the word oaten

explanation.surface: A cook sends a lad for eggs stuffed with oats as fillings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' anagrams SENT LAD into DENTALS; 'eggs' is a verb, not food.
explanation.definitionFit: These practitioners fill cavities in teeth, a playful sense of the definition.

clue.text: Spinning Sid replaces Rolling Ric in Big Top event

indicators.note: replaces says one set of letters is swapped in for another inside the word

parts.note: the big top is the tent of a circus, standing for the circus itself
rolling means the name Ric is tumbled into a new order, giving the opening letters of the circus word
spinning means the name Sid is whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Two performers, Sid and Ric, take turns spinning and rolling at a circus show.
explanation.walkthrough: Both names are scrambled: 'Rolling' and 'Spinning' are the anagram signals, so the swap happens between the jumbled versions, not the names as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing the heavy disc is a field event in athletics, so the name of the implement names the contest.

clue.text: Doctrinaire hides gold, rogues discovered

indicators.note: discovered means each word loses its covering, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dogmatic person hides gold, but the rogues are found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' looks like 'found', but read as dis-covered it strips each word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire person rigidly follows a theory, the mark of a dogmatic zealot.

clue.text: Depression engulfs husband with chronic ear infection

indicators.note: engulfs means the dip word swallows the husband letter

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between mountains

indicators.note: chronic, meaning very bad, signals that the letters of ear are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wife's depression grows as her husband suffers a chronic ear infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an acute bacterial disease of the intestine.

clue.text: Indicated variety of wheat

definitions.meaning: spelled out or signified, as in 'that spelled trouble'
an ancient hardy grain related to common wheat

explanation.surface: A sign pointed out a particular strain of wheat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a past form of spell, meaning signified, and also names an old grain species.

clue.text: Post retired doctors on Syrian transport storing mineral mostly

indicators.note: retired means the doctors' body is drawn back, read in the other direction

parts.note: the BMA is the British Medical Association, the doctors' body

indicators.note: storing means the leader's name and vessel hold the mineral inside

parts.note: Assad was the ruling family name in Syria
a ship is a means of transport

indicators.note: mostly means losing the last letter

parts.note: ore is a mineral source of metal

explanation.surface: Retired doctors post supplies on a Syrian ship carrying most of a cargo of ore.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic post is a position held, such as the office of envoy to a foreign state.

clue.text: Lack of drive space with one unit regularly

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of space, half an em

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words one unit

explanation.surface: A sluggish engine lacking push, with only a unit of space and a single part working.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless boredom, a state with no motivation or energy to act.

clue.text: Main nationalist colour on side of saltire

parts.note: umber is a brown earth colour

indicators.note: side of here means the final edge letter of the word saltire

explanation.surface: A Scottish nationalist's main colour sits on the side of the saltire flag.
explanation.walkthrough: The saltire is the white diagonal cross of Scotland's flag, which suits the nationalist surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Main and number one both describe the chief or principal item.

clue.text: Exchange coin inside of Asian capital

indicators.note: exchange means the letters of coin are swapped around into a new order
inside of means the inner letters of Asian, dropping its first and last

explanation.surface: A traveller swaps coins in the middle of an Asian capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Fragment in meal, time for complaint

indicators.note: to fragment is to break apart, so the letters of in meal are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner finds a fragment in the meal and, in time, makes a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fragment' reads as a noun, a bit found in food, but it is a verb signalling the anagram of IN MEAL into AILMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or disorder.

clue.text: English call for help to restrict media shots

indicators.note: to restrict means the distress signal hems in the media word

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
the press is the news media

explanation.surface: An Englishman calls for help to restrict the media taking photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a single small serving of strong coffee, so these are coffee shots.

clue.text: Filename left encrypted at home

indicators.note: encrypted means the letters are scrambled into code

explanation.surface: A computer file is left encrypted on the home machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase describes doing something in the family circle, privately at one's own residence.

clue.text: Close to confiscating girl's flute?

indicators.note: close to means the final letter of the word confiscating

parts.note: a lass is a girl; the 's joins girl to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone is about to confiscate a girl's flute.
explanation.walkthrough: The flute looks like the instrument, but the question mark flags it as a tall wine glass, a champagne flute.
explanation.definitionFit: A champagne flute is a tall narrow drinking vessel, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Quiet anger about tattoo's reduction in size

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

indicators.note: about means the anger word goes round the tattoo word

parts.note: rage is fierce anger
ink is slang for a tattoo

explanation.surface: Someone quietly fumes as their tattoo shrinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrinkage is the amount by which something contracts or gets smaller.

clue.text: Person taking temperature before head cold cleared

indicators.note: cleared means the cold letter is removed from the leader word

parts.note: a chief is the head of a group
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A patient with a head cold has their temperature taken before it clears up.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber or pilferer is someone who takes what belongs to others.

clue.text: Undelivered sample of store tunics brought back

indicators.note: brought back says the hidden letters are read backwards
sample of says a run of letters is taken from inside the words store tunics

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sample from a shop's stock of tunics is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'sample' in the definition, but 'sample of' is the hiding signal and 'Undelivered' alone means not yet born; without it the hidden step has no indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means within the womb, describing a baby not yet born.

clue.text: Soviet stockpiler in US runs out for vegetable

parts.note: red describes a Soviet communist

indicators.note: out means the runs letter is dropped from the stockpiler word

parts.note: a prepper, in American usage, stockpiles supplies for disaster
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Soviet hoarder in America runs out of supplies, leaving only vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsicum such as a ripe bell variety is a common salad vegetable.

clue.text: Words of wisdom from one who tests Britain

parts.note: a prover is someone who tests or proves things

explanation.surface: A wise saying from a British examiner.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short traditional saying expressing a general truth.

clue.text: Local black drink that is on front of magazine

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
rum is a spirit

indicators.note: front of means the opening letter of the word magazine

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A dark drink is placed on the cover of a local magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: A Brummie is someone from Birmingham, England's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: A local is a native resident of a place, here a native of Birmingham.

clue.text: Award sailor returning to guard rear of vessel

indicators.note: to guard means the reversed sailor letters surround the stern word
returning means the seaman letters come back reversed

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
aft is the rear part of a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor goes back to guard the stern of the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A BAFTA is a prize from the British Academy of Film and Television Arts.

clue.text: 75% of stone floor gets abrasive treatment

indicators.note: 75% of means three of the four letters of the gem word are kept, from the front

parts.note: a ruby is a precious stone
to floor someone is to knock them down

explanation.surface: A stone floor gets most of the scrubbing and harsh treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage or vigorous rubbing with a towel is a rough, friction-based treatment.

clue.text: User of stakes for fence initially blocks purchase

indicators.note: blocks means that letter sits inside the purchase word, obstructing it

parts.note: to buy is to purchase

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of the words for and fence

explanation.surface: Someone buying wooden stakes for a fence finds the first lot blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: Buffy the Vampire Slayer, the TV heroine, kills vampires with wooden stakes; 'stakes' tempts towards betting or fencing posts.
explanation.definitionFit: The television vampire slayer famously dispatches her foes with a wooden stake through the heart.

clue.text: Joyful church hosts dance affair without strings

indicators.note: hosts means the outer pair of pieces take in the dance word

parts.note: fun, used as an adjective, means enjoyable or joyful
a reel is a lively Scottish dance

explanation.surface: A cheerful church holds a dance with no conditions attached.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names something given apparently at no cost or obligation, an event with no catch.

clue.text: Waste year in pursuit of fellow goddess

indicators.note: in pursuit of means the rearranged letters come behind the fellow letter
waste means the letters of year are ruined and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wastes a year chasing a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Freya is the Norse deity of love and fertility.

clue.text: Cut-throat maybe exposed on small island chain

indicators.note: exposed means the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: a cut-throat is a type of open-bladed shaving razor
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A cut-throat villain is exposed on a small island chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut-throat' suggests a murderer, but it is the straight razor, and 'exposed' strips its outer letters to leave AZO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Azores are a Portuguese archipelago in the mid-Atlantic.

clue.text: Due to put enclosure around twisted tree

indicators.note: around means the enclosure word wraps the turned tree

parts.note: a pale is a fenced area or enclosure

indicators.note: twisted means the tree word is turned so it reads the other way

parts.note: a bay is a laurel tree

explanation.surface: It is time to build a fence around a gnarled tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill that is due is owing and must be settled.
